A1.justification: Both complete 27-page PDFs describe the same Orthogonal Residual Update study. Sections 1–5 and Appendices A–F, including equations, tables, figures and code listings, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-classification experiments with ViTs and ResNetV2 models in Table 2, alongside ablations and internal-dynamics analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the original classification results, ablations and internal-dynamics analyses reported in v1.

M1.justification: The orthogonal residual update, feature-wise and global procedures, stability constant and implementation remain unchanged in Section 3, Algorithms 1–2 and Appendix F.

E1.justification: Both versions use CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, TinyImageNet and ImageNet-1k for image classification, retaining the same evaluated coverage and test scenarios.

E2.justification: The same Linear/Identity baselines and orthogonal-update configurations participate in the main comparisons, connection-switching experiments, initialization study and LayerNorm study. No comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendices A and C retain identical datasets, splits, metrics, model configurations, training budgets, preprocessing and connection-switching protocols.

E4.justification: The connection-switching, update-probability, layer-placement, epsilon, initialization and final-LayerNorm analyses are unchanged. Sections 3.5 and Appendix D also retain the same internal-norm analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same run counts, mean-and-standard-deviation reporting, error bars and Pearson correlation tests. The three-run exceptions and five-run experiments are documented identically.

E6.justification: All reported numerical results and plotted findings match. For example, Table 2 reports ViT-B ImageNet-1k accuracy of 71.09 ± 0.32% for Linear and 75.45 ± 0.12% for Orthogonal-F in both versions; appendix results also remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The decomposition and gradient equations, Appendix B derivations and proof discussion, and Appendix E definitions and calculations of the width-to-depth ratio are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about novel representational directions, generalization, stability and learning efficiency, including the stated +4.3 percentage-point ImageNet-1k gain.

C2.justification: Both retain the same interpretations of norm dynamics, connection switching and architectural width-to-depth effects. The limitations concerning computational resources, model scale and validation beyond image classification are unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains identical hyperparameters, augmentation settings, hardware and training times. Appendix F's code and implementation explanations are unchanged; its highlighting change supplies no new technical information.

R1.justification: The same 38 references and related-work discussion remain, including the positioning against skip-path modifications, orthogonal initialization, orthogonality constraints and orthogonal finetuning.

P1.justification: The first-page author name changes from Younjae Yu to Youngjae Yu, and the preprint footer becomes a NeurIPS 2025 conference footer. The arXiv stamp is updated; substantive prose and document organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Appendix F's Listings 1–2 change docstring highlighting from gray to orange. Figures 1–10, Tables 1–11, captions and placement remain unchanged, making this a limited visual-formatting revision.

improvement.justification: v2 updates author and publication information and code highlighting, while retaining the same scientific content, evidence, explanations, limitations and reproducibility details throughout the appendices. These limited editorial and visual changes produce no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
